title: MSMEs are 99.6% of Philippine businesses
hook: 99.6% of Philippine businesses are MSMEs. How many have been in the news? 🤔
cta: Tag a negosyante whose story deserves coverage

slides.label: of Philippine *businesses*
slides.body: And they generate **66.97%** of all jobs. That's a lot of untold business stories.
slides.sub: May kwento ka? Write the release

captions_meta.hook: 99.6% of Philippine businesses are MSMEs. How many have been in the news? 🤔
lines: New branches, first exports, 50 new hires: these are real news stories.
They just rarely get written in a format newsrooms can use.
captions_meta.li_hook:
MSMEs make up 99.6% of Philippine businesses and generate 66.97% of jobs.
Their share of business headlines is a fraction of that.
li_body: DTI's 2023 figures (1,246,373 enterprises, 6,351,466 MSME jobs) are usually quoted in policy discussions. We read them as a communications gap: more than a million businesses with stories that never reach a reporter.

Not because they lack news value, but because they aren't packaged as news. A third branch in Davao, a first export order or 50 new hires is a strong local story when it comes with clear numbers and a quotable spokesperson.
captions_meta.li_close: If you run an MSME: which story from this year should the public hear?
captions_meta.fb: Fun fact: 99.6% of businesses in the Philippines are MSMEs. If yours is one of them, your story deserves coverage too 💙
